attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion in his own post, introducing his experiments with Southen.

semantics.note: Capability claim about DALL-E via Bing: infringement can occur with no intent to infringe and no name in the prompt. Here 'can' states a capability, not a probability hedge. Both conditions are kept.

contract.note: Reading it as a capability claim tied to the December 2023 Bing deployment is ordinary. Requiring evidence of infringing circumstances, and not just resemblance, matches the word 'infringement'. The intent requirement turns on interpretation.

evidence.note: June 2024 preprint showing that name-free prompts produce copyrighted characters and that DALL-E prompt rewriting falls short. It is later than the target period, does not test December Bing, and makes no infringement or intent finding.

reviews.rationale: The only item is later research about a different period. It shows the general risk but not the December 2023 Bing behavior with a non-deliberate user and an infringing output. Nothing contradicts the claim. The packet does not settle it.

attribution.note: Marcus's own bulleted assertion in his post.

semantics.note: Faithful past-tense claim that DALL-E and ChatGPT were trained on copyrighted material. It makes no claim about whether that use was lawful.

contract.note: Counting licensed copyrighted material matches the literal words, which say nothing about authorization. Requiring both product families to be covered is fair.

evidence.note: Oct 2022 Shutterstock release quoting OpenAI's CEO: licensed Shutterstock imagery was critical to training DALL-E. These are licensed contributor works, i.e. copyrighted material. It is an admission, dated before the post.
June 2023 OpenAI disclosure: ChatGPT training data includes licensed content. Licensing implies copyright-protected material. Dated before the post.
May 2023 CRS report relaying OpenAI's acknowledgment that its programs train on datasets including copyrighted works. It is a secondary summary about earlier systems, so it corroborates only.

reviews.rationale: OpenAI's own pre-post admissions say licensed copyrighted material was used to train both DALL-E (Shutterstock) and ChatGPT (licensed content). These statements cut against the company's interest. No evidence shows either system was trained without copyrighted material.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion describing his and Southen's Bing experiments.

semantics.note: Capability claim that DALL-E, accessed through Bing, can reproduce sources verbatim or near-verbatim. The Bing qualifier is kept.

contract.note: Reading 'verbatim and near-verbatim repetition of sources' as close reproduction of identifiable source images is ordinary. Mere character resemblance would be a looser claim. The ambiguity is flagged, and the reading decides what evidence counts.

evidence.note: Jan 2024 Tom's Hardware tests in which Bing produced Mario and Sonic from generic prompts. Test dates are unspecified, and there is no comparison with a particular source image. That shows character resemblance, not near-verbatim copying.

reviews.rationale: No independent, dated December 2023 Bing output is matched to an identifiable source image. The one demonstration shows only character generation. Nothing contradicts the claim. Unresolved on this packet.

attribution.note: Marcus himself asserts the 'not fully reliable' part. He attributes the existence of name-blocking to reports ('reportedly'), but endorses it as the premise.

semantics.note: Faithful: a name-blocking safeguard exists but is not fully reliable. The Bing context is supplied by the contract rather than the proposition, which is acceptable.

contract.note: The contract asks for at least one failure within the safeguard's intended coverage during December 2023 on Bing. That is a fair, ordinary reading of 'aren't fully reliable'. Coverage of the safeguard is unspecified, so interpretation matters.

evidence.note: Nov 2023 Register report: Bing temporarily blocked 'Disney', then lifted the ban with output restrictions. It shows a name safeguard existed and changed. It is from November and shows no December failure or success, so it neither supports nor contradicts the claim.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows a Bing name-blocking measure in November 2023, but no dated December record of a failure within its coverage. The Disney item does not establish full reliability, so it does not contradict the claim. Unresolved.
